intent: Extract Spring Boot fat JARs before training
extract Spring Boot JARs with the target JDK

title: extract Spring Boot fat JARs with -Djarmode=tools, run by the target JDK
why: CDS and AOT archives cannot reference classes inside nested JARs, so a Spring Boot fat JAR must be unpacked before training (PR 26). Running the extraction with the target JDK uses the same JVM that will run the application later.
alternative: Plain ZIP extraction. Issue 3 lists it as a fallback. It is not used for Spring Boot.

title: use other executable JARs unchanged; no ZIP fallback
why: A shaded or uber JAR already runs and can be archived as it is. Unzipping it would only change the classpath and would not help (PR 26). This differs from the wording of issue 3, and the PR says so.
alternative: The plain-ZIP fallback that issue 3 asked for.

title: reject Spring Boot older than 3.3 before running anything
why: The tools jarmode does not exist before Spring Boot 3.3 (PR 26). The check reads Spring-Boot-Version from the manifest and gives a clear message instead of a failed process.
alternative: Run the extraction and report its failure. The failure message also mentions the 3.3 requirement as a second guard.

title: detect Spring Boot from the JAR manifest
why: Inferred from the code: the Spring-Boot-Version attribute, or a Main-Class under org.springframework.boot.loader, identifies a Spring Boot JAR without starting a process. The PR does not state a reason.

title: extract only into an empty or absent directory
why: PR 26 states that nothing is overwritten. A non-empty destination is an error.
alternative: Delete and recreate the destination. No record of this being considered.

title: run external commands through an injectable CommandRunner
why: The extraction logic can then be unit tested without starting Spring (PR 26). The default runner starts a real process and kills it after a timeout.
alternative: Call ProcessBuilder directly in JarExtractor. Unknown whether it was considered.

name: JarExtractor
role: Classifies a JAR from its manifest and prepares it for training: Spring Boot JARs are extracted into a runnable JAR plus lib/, other executable JARs are used as they are
conditions: Spring Boot 3.3 or later; destination must be empty or absent; expects exactly one top-level .jar in the destination after extraction

name: CommandRunner
role: Runs an external command and returns the exit code and merged output
conditions: Default implementation kills the process after a timeout; tests replace it with a fake

name: build command --jar and --work-dir
role: Prepares the JAR and extracts into work-dir/app (default .mnemo-warmup)
conditions: Exit code 2 when the JAR is missing or not valid

subject: Extraction layout never confirmed on a real Spring Boot app
why: The code assumes that tools extract writes one JAR with a Class-Path to lib/. PR 26 says this was not checked against a real Spring Boot run, because no demo app could be built in the sandbox. An opt-in test with -Dwarmup.test.springBootJar can check it.
